title: High-resolution Imaging of Nuclear Dynamics in Live Cells under Uniaxial Tensile Strain
protocol: Design a single-well polydimethylsiloxane mold for high-resolution imaging.
Keep the overall plate dimensions at 60 mm x 73 mm.
Create a cell compartment of 23 mm x 23 mm square.
Maintain the depth of the cell compartment to no more than 80 μm.
Raise the cell compartment on a square pedestal with a height of 3 mm.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane base and curing agent in a ratio of 20:1 by weight.
Weigh a total of 20 g of polydimethylsiloxane for making one plate mold or 150 g for making square compartments.
Place the mixture in a vacuum degasser at -0.8 bar for 30 minutes to remove bubbles.
Pour the degassed mixture into molds for plates or into 150 mm plastic dishes for square compartments.
Remove additional bubbles by blowing air or using vacuum degassing again at -0.8 bar for 30 minutes.
Place the molds or dishes in an 80 °C oven on a leveling table for 2 hours.
Carefully remove the molds or dishes from the oven and let them cool to room temperature.
Gently peel out the cured polydimethylsiloxane after carefully cutting the edges with a blade.
Draw a 2 cm x 2 cm grid on a 150 mm-diameter polydimethylsiloxane plate with a marker.
Within each square of the grid, draw a 1 cm x 1 cm inner square.
Cut along the lines to obtain individual square compartments using a blade.
Incubate the polydimethylsiloxane plates and compartments in 100% acetone for 4 hours.
Incubate them in 100% ethanol for 4 hours.
Incubate them in autoclaved water for 4 hours.
Place the plates on paraffin film backing paper inside a 150 mm diameter plastic dish.
Dry the polydimethylsiloxane plate in an 80 °C oven for 4 hours.
Seal the dishes containing the polydimethylsiloxane plates and compartments with paraffin film.
Store the sealed dishes in a cold room until further use.
Remove the paraffin film from the stored dishes.
Place the polydimethylsiloxane plates under ultraviolet light for 30 minutes.
Plasma-treat the polydimethylsiloxane plates (cell compartment facing up) at 150 W for 5 minutes without the square compartments.
Immediately place the square compartments onto the plasma-treated surface and press manually to stick them temporarily.
Do not plasma-treat square compartments.
Add 200 µL of 100 mM (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane to the well for 2 h.
Wash the wells 3 times with deionized water after incubation.
Weigh 2 mg of bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate and dissolve it in 700 µL of 1 M (4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethane sulfonic acid buffer, pH 8.0, and 2.8 mL of water.
Add 135 µL of the bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate solution and 15 µL of 1 mg/mL fibronectin to each well in the polydimethylsiloxane plate for 4 h at room temperature.
Wash the wells 3 times with phosphate-buffered saline after addition of fibronectin.
Add 500 µL of phosphate-buffered saline solution to the well.
Cover the dish containing the polydimethylsiloxane with paraffin film.
Store the dish in a cold room until further use.
Incubate plastic dishes and flasks with a 5 µg/mL solution of poly-D-lysine (PDL) for 1 h.
Add 1.5 mL of PDL solution per 35 mm-diameter dish.
Add 3 mL of PDL solution per 60 mm-diameter dish.
Add 10 mL of PDL solution per 75 cm² culture flask.
Wash the dishes and flasks twice with sterile water.
Leave the dishes and flasks to dry in the biosafety cabinet for 1 h or until completely dry.
Store the dried dishes and flasks at 4 °C until further use.
Prepare 50 mL of 100x solutions of proliferation and differentiation medium for murine oligodendrocyte progenitor cells.
Make aliquots of 2.5 mL from the prepared solution.
Store the aliquoted solutions at -80 °C.
Dissolve 510 mg of bovine serum albumin in 17 mL of Dulbecco’s medium.
Dissolve 310 μg of progesterone in 31 µL of ethanol.
Dissolve 80 mg of putrescine in 500 µL of Dulbecco’s medium.
Dissolve 25 µg of sodium selenite in 10 µL of Dulbecco’s medium.
Add the dissolved components to full DMEM up to a total volume of 50 mL.
Dissolve 2 mg of triiodothyronine in 40 μL of sodium hydroxide.
Dissolve 2 mg of L-thyroxine in 40 μL of sodium hydroxide.
Fill up the solution to 50 mL with Dulbecco’s medium.
Filter the solution through a sterile disposable filter unit.
Aliquot and store the aliquots at -80°C.
Mix 2.5 mL of 100x solution of proliferation/differentiation medium with 12.5 mg of holo-transferrin, 125 μL of 10 mg/mL insulin, and 2.5 mL of 100x penicillin-streptomycin.
Fill up the solution to 250 mL with Dulbecco’s medium.
Filter it through a sterile disposable filter unit.
Start with oligodendrocyte progenitor cells suspended in proliferation medium.
Seed these cells at a density of 35,000 cells/cm² onto PDL-coated plastic surfaces.
Adjust the volume of the proliferation medium to 3 mL per 10 cm² of surface area of plastic substratum.
Add growth factors every day at a concentration of 10 ng/mL.
Change half of the proliferation medium on alternate days.
On the third day, remove the medium from the cells.
Wash the cell culture dish or flask once with phosphate-buffered saline solution.
Add 1 mL of gentle cell detachment solution per 20 cm² area.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 minutes.
Gently tap the dish or flask to detach all cells.
Pipette using a 200 µL tip to break clumps into single cells.
Transfer detached cells to a 50 mL tube.
Dilute cells in proliferation medium.
Spin at 0.2 x g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in proliferation medium to make a total volume of 1 mL.
Count the cells using a cytometer.
Wash fibronectin-functionalized polydimethylsiloxane plates twice with proliferation medium, each wash lasting 15 minutes.
Seed 35,000 cells per polydimethylsiloxane plate in 700 µL of proliferation medium.
Add 1.4 µL of CellLight H2B-GFP BacMam2 transfection mix for histone H2B labeling with green fluorescent protein.
Mount the polydimethylsiloxane samples with cells on a uniaxial strain device after 24 hours.
Change the medium in all samples to differentiation medium.
Measure the unstrained cell compartment length.
Increase the cell compartment length by the desired amount using the stage micrometer screw.
Place the stretched and unstretched polydimethylsiloxane samples in the incubator at 37 °C.
Turn on the microscope.
Set the microscope incubator temperature to 37 °C.
Position the 100x oil immersion objective to the central position.
Unscrew and reassemble the objective with an objective ring.
Add a drop of oil if using an oil objective.
Prepare a holder via 3D printing or machining, featuring an angled window and a step.
Place a thickness #0 glass coverslip on the holder's window filled with medium.
Position the strain device in an inverted state for imaging.
Place a glass coverslip with dimensions of 25 mm x 25 mm or 35 mm in diameter onto the holder.
Spread vacuum grease at the periphery of the window using the glass coverslip.
Tape the plastic window onto the microscope stage.
Screw a z-translation stage onto the microscope stage and move it to the topmost z-position.
Remove 500 µL of medium from the stretched polydimethylsiloxane plate.
Add the removed medium onto the glass coverslip in the white plastic window.
Carefully detach the square compartment from the polydimethylsiloxane plate using sterile tweezers.
Hold the strain device upright with cells facing up above the white plastic window.
Invert the strain device so that extra medium drops directly into the middle of the glass coverslip (cells facing down).
Place the bottom part of the strain device onto the z-translation stage with double-sided tape.
While looking through the eyepiece under brightfield, slowly bring the strain device down by lowering the z-translation stage.
Move the objective up to focus on the cells, performing this step extremely slowly and carefully.
Scan the polydimethylsiloxane plate in x- and y-directions to find a cell with a fluorescent nucleus under epifluorescence with 488 nm wavelength excitation.
Check if the lateral displacement of the microscope stage affects vertical focusing significantly.
Select multiple regions of interest using a multipoint feature on the software when focusing is not sensitive to lateral displacement.
Image one cell at a time when focusing is very sensitive to any lateral displacement of the stage.
Mark the x-, y-, and z-positions for each cell of interest.
Record wide-field images of the nucleus with 488 nm wavelength excitation at intervals of 30 seconds per frame.
Record brightfield images of the cell at intervals of 30 seconds per frame.
Open the sequence of nucleus images in an image analysis software.
Threshold the nucleus time-lapse images using a threshold command in ImageJ or Graythresh command in MATLAB.
Get the nucleus area as a function of time from the thresholded images.
Plot the nucleus area over time in a data plotting software.
Fit a third order polynomial to the plotted data using Analysis | Fitting | Polynomial Fit command in Origin or Polyfit command in MATLAB.
Subtract the value of the fitted polynomial from the actual area for each time point.
Calculate the corrected area, known as the residual area.
